reference: GNU coreutils head in the isolated reference environment. Bash type/help metadata follows the documented builtin options and is counted separately.
coverage: Explicit line and byte prefixes, including embedded NUL bytes.
Negative line counts with an unterminated final record.
Default, quiet, and forced single-file headers across multiple files.
GNU binary suffix count, option permutation, and -- option termination.
Malformed count failure status and diagnostics presence.
Seekable stdin consumption followed by a Bash read.
Bash builtin type and help metadata contracts.
exclusions: The documented positive-line repeated '-' pipe case intentionally preserves bytes that GNU head may read ahead; it is not compared as GNU parity.
Signals, live input mutation, write-failure injection, large streaming workloads, cross-libc behavior, and full GNU option coverage are outside this focused suite.
The type/help cases validate Bash metadata only and do not count as head operation coverage. No operation requires a privileged VM or mock, so no deferred cases are needed.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Copies two newline-delimited records and leaves a following unterminated record out of the output.
Checks byte-count mode against data containing an embedded NUL and newline.
Negative line count excludes the trailing unterminated record while preserving earlier complete records.
Uses NUL as the record delimiter and copies exactly the first two records.
Checks default headers for two named operands and quiet suppression over both operands.
cases.script:
printf 'first
more
' > one
printf 'second
more
' > two
head -n 1 one two
head --quiet -n 1 one two

cases.purpose: Forces a filename header for one input operand.
Checks GNU's 1K binary byte suffix at the 1024-byte boundary.
Checks option permutation after an operand and -- handling for a relative filename beginning with a dash.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
' > input
printf 'dash
more
' > -input
head input -n 2
head -n 1 -- -input

cases.purpose: A malformed line count must fail before producing file data and emit a diagnostic.
After reading one line from seekable stdin, a Bash read sees the next line, validating exact input consumption.
Bash type -t must identify the registered head command as a builtin.
Bash help must expose the documented --lines and --bytes options for this builtin.
cases.script: help head | { lines=0; bytes=0; while IFS= read -r line; do case $line in *--lines=*) lines=1;; esac; case $line in *--bytes=*) bytes=1;; esac; done; printf 'lines=%s bytes=%s\n' "$lines" "$bytes"; }

cases.purpose: Zero counts emit nothing; tail-excluding byte mode handles binary data and a count larger than the input.
cases.script:
printf 'ab\000cd\n' > input
head -n 0 input
head -c 0 input
head -c -2 input
head -c -99 input

cases.purpose: A missing first operand must not hide the bytes from a later valid file or erase aggregate failure.
